comments.text: Exposed by fz-hwn.27.6 (A). A joined OPAQUE POLYMORPHIC callable — ty (a0,a1)->a2#add_a | (a0,a1)->a2#add_b — boxes correctly at its definition (shape_for_local_value sees is_callable=true -> boxed CallableDescr{function:None, capture_lanes:[value_lane]}) but is SUPPLIED scalar downstream: native.rs:2756 encode_runtime_value errors 'attempted to encode callable shape ShapeId(24) for value ValueId(2) from Transport{shape:17, lanes:[Var(2)]}'. The transport plan assigned value 2 inconsistent shapes across producer (boxed 24) and the bound value (scalar Lane 17). Fixture comment documents prior identical regression: 'joined value reached the reducer loop as a scalar word'. VERIFIED independent of phantom_resolution_keys (disabling the ghost filter does not change it) -> it is the core whole-scope addressing of the joined callable's two same-shape/different-tag clauses interacting with the boxing seam (fz-hwn.22 subsystem / [[fz_callable_boxing_seam]]). Lib is 2240/0 green; ONLY this fixture (matrix opaque_fn_value_join build/run/interp) fails. Next: trace where value 2 is bound scalar (transport input vs local-value vs join source position) and unify it to the boxed shape. Repro: target/debug/fz2 build fixtures2/behavior/opaque_fn_value_join.fz -o /tmp/o.o

CORRECTION: NON-DETERMINISTIC. The lib test compiler2_native_program_joins_callable_resume_before_materializing_closure_call is FLAKY (observed FAIL/ok/FAIL/FAIL across 4 runs) — SAME bug as the matrix opaque_fn_value_join (which fails consistently, larger path). So lib is NOT cleanly green: it is 2239-2240/0-1 depending on run. The flakiness => a HashMap (unordered) iteration in the shape-derivation / boxing-seam path makes value 2's producer-vs-consumer shape sometimes align (pass) sometimes not (fail). STRONG LEAD: find the unordered iteration in transport shape derivation for the joined opaque callable (generic_callable_shape_with_resolutions / boundary publication / value_lane) and make it ordered (BTreeMap or sort) — likely fixes both deterministically. Repro flaky: loop 'cargo test --lib compiler2::drive_test::compiler2_native_program_joins_callable_resume_before_materializing_closure_call'.

ROOT CAUSE (traced to ground). add_a/add_b have IDENTICAL signatures (x,acc)->acc+x; reducer = add_a|add_b is a join of two same-arrow functions distinguished only by ClosureLit fn tag (#31/#32). The SAME reducer value is represented TWO inconsistent ways: value 10 (local case-join in main, built from closure_lit, alpha'd separately, NOT re-addressed) = (a0,a1)->a2#31 | (a3,a4)->a5#32 (DISTINCT-arrow clauses); value 2 (same reducer as the Enum.reduce arg, re-addressed by address_inputs as a key input under Param(2)) = (a0,a1)->a2#31 | (a0,a1)->a2#32 (IDENTICAL-arrow clauses). MECHANISM: address_remap_children addresses by structural PATH; both clauses of a func-union sit at the SAME path (funcs axis at Param(2)), so clause-#31.arg0 and clause-#32.arg0 get the SAME address => the two arrows COLLAPSE to identical (only the ClosureLit tag survives). So the same value has a distinct-arrow type at its producer and a same-arrow type at its consumer => shape mismatch (encode boxed shape 24 from scalar 17). MASKED at HEAD because conflation gave EVERY position spuriously-distinct arrows, so producer/consumer happened to agree. The non-determinism (lib flaky) falls out: identical-arrow-different-tag clauses make any downstream order/select keyed on the arrow ambiguous between #31/#32 => order-dependent; fz2 build (fuller path) deterministically hits the bad pairing. FIX (not a defect in A — A is correct): canonicalize closure/fn-ref VALUE types the SAME way at every position so value 10 == value 2 byte-identical. Either (a) extend canonical-by-construction to closure value types (local join already addressed), or (b) stop address_inputs collapsing a function-VALUE arg's internal arrows. Principled = consistency. Repro deterministic: target/debug/fz2 build fixtures2/behavior/opaque_fn_value_join.fz -o /tmp/o.o

FIX ATTEMPT 1 (REVERTED — wrong). Tried: skip re-addressing closure-LITERAL arrows in address_remap_children (if sig.lit.is_some() continue), reasoning closure_var_id vars are already canonical-per-function. RESULT: turned the deterministic build-fail into FLAKY (build run1 PASS run2 FAIL run3 PASS) — i.e. fixed the value2/value10 arrow inconsistency but exposed a SECOND non-determinism — AND regressed 5 lib tests (enum_reduce backend/jit, compile_root aot/jit, native_program_keeps_distinct_direct_callable_executables_for_same_surface_when_capture_identity_differs). LEARNING: closure arrows MUST be addressed for dispatch (value 2 addressed is CORRECT; those 5 tests rely on it). So the fix is NOT 'skip addressing' — it is to make CONSTRUCTION consistent too: value 10 (the local closure value, built by fn_ref_lit/closure_lit with closure_var_id(fn_id,pos)=fn_id*64+pos, fn_id-keyed distinct-per-function vars, NEVER re-addressed) must be canonicalized the SAME way as value 2 (addressed). Option (a): fn_ref_lit/closure_lit emit ADDRESSED arrows (param_alpha/result_alpha) so same-arity functions share one arrow distinguished only by the ClosureLit tag — but this changes the fundamental closure_var_id scheme (see lit_set.rs:128-151 comment: fn_id-keying gives consistent ret var across arities + no cross-function aliasing) so it is wide/risky and needs careful design + full AOT/JIT/interp verification. SECOND non-determinism (separate): the opaque join has TWO producers (add_a #31, add_b #32) that, once their surfaces coincide, are matched/ordered via HashMap iteration (contexts.iter().find at transport.rs:2419/2930; callable_flows.values() at 2096) — order-dependent. Both must be addressed for 27.12. A's conflation work is correct and intact (lib 2240/0 when the flaky test rolls pass).
